profile.summary: Protenix is an open-source biomolecular structure predictor from ByteDance, built as a reproduction of AlphaFold3. It takes a JSON description of the molecules in a complex, such as protein chains, ligands and nucleic acids, optionally with multiple sequence alignments and templates, and predicts the all-atom three-dimensional structure of the complex. It is run through a command-line tool that also prepares the alignment and template inputs.

summary_quotes.text: we present Protenix, a comprehensive reproduction of AlphaFold3 (AF3), aimed at advancing the field of biomolecular structure prediction
Protenix tackles the challenges of predicting complex interactions involving proteins, ligands, and nucleic acids
# Predict structure using a JSON input
Protenix provides a unified CLI for structure prediction, data preprocessing, and database searching.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Protenix follows the AlphaFold3 design: a diffusion model that samples atom coordinates, with recycling over a pairformer trunk and a confidence head. Inference is controlled by the number of recycles and the number of diffusion steps: the base checkpoints use 10 recycles and 200 diffusion steps, while the mini and tiny checkpoints use 4 recycles and 5 steps to run faster. Most checkpoints take multiple sequence alignments; the v1.0.0 checkpoints also take RNA alignments and structural templates, the constraint checkpoint takes pocket and contact restraints, and the ESM and ISM checkpoints add single-sequence protein language model embeddings from ESM2-3B (standard ESM2 embeddings for ESM, ISM embeddings for ISM) and do not use alignments by default.
sections.source_locator: supported_models.md: Model Detailed Descriptions; instructions: Key Inference Flags, Inference Cost

quotes.text: **Characteristics**: Significant reduction in parameters and faster inference speed.
Integrates the single-sequence protein language model (ESM2-3B), performing better when MSAs are unavailable.
**Characteristics**: Allows incorporating additional experimental constraints during inference (e.g., Pocket, Contact).
the `SampleDiffusion` and `ConfidenceHead` modules are executed in full-precision (FP32) to maintain numerical stability and prediction accuracy
**Difference**: `ESM` uses standard ESM2 embeddings, while `ISM` uses specific ISM embeddings.
**Note**: For efficiency, these models do not use MSA by default.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository lists nine named checkpoints. Their names follow the pattern protenix_{model_size}_{features}_{version}, with sizes base, mini and tiny. The base v1.0.0 checkpoints hold 368.48 M parameters; protenix-v2 holds 464.44 M, mini 135.22 M or 134.06 M, and tiny 109.50 M. Two training data cutoffs exist: 2021-09-30, chosen to match AlphaFold3, and 2025-06-30 for the applied checkpoint. A result must name the checkpoint, because accuracy, cutoff and inference settings all differ between them, and should also name the number of seeds and samples, since the README reports accuracy rising with the sampling budget.

quotes.text: **model_size**: Size of the model, including `base`, `mini` (lightweight), and `tiny` (minimal).
Base model, trained with a data cutoff aligned with AlphaFold3 (2021-09-30).
Applied model, trained with an updated data cutoff (2025-06-30) for better practical performance.
increasing the sampling budget from several to hundreds of candidates leads to consistent log-linear gains

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: All-atom biomolecular structure predictor, a diffusion model reproducing AlphaFold3.

quotes.text: Protenix is built for high-accuracy structure prediction.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: AlphaFold3-style pairformer trunk with recycling, a diffusion sampler and a confidence head. Base checkpoints run 10 recycles and 200 diffusion steps; mini and tiny run 4 recycles and 5 steps. Protenix-v2 raises the representation dimension (c_z=256).
facts.source_locator: supported_models.md: Model Detailed Descriptions; instructions: Inference Cost, training arguments

quotes.text: `SampleDiffusion`, `ConfidenceHead`, `Mini-rollout`, and `Loss` parts remain in FP32 for stability

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A JSON file naming the chains of the complex, for example a proteinChain with its sequence, count and modifications, plus covalent bonds. Multiple sequence alignments, RNA alignments and templates are prepared by the same tool and referenced from the JSON. PDB and CIF files can be converted to this JSON.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Predicted structures with confidence estimates, written to the output directory given on the command line. One or more samples per input, controlled by the seeds and the sample count.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 368.48 M (protenix_base_default_v1.0.0 and protenix_base_20250630_v1.0.0), 464.44 M (protenix-v2), 368.09 M and 368.30 M (the v0.5.0 base and constraint checkpoints), 135.22 M (mini ESM and ISM), 134.06 M (mini default), 109.50 M (tiny default).

facts.value: The wwPDB dataset, with the preprocessing and MSA pipelines released in the repository. The download needs at least 1.5T of disk space.

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: 2021-09-30 for every checkpoint except protenix_base_20250630_v1.0.0, whose cutoff is 2025-06-30. The 2021-09-30 cutoff was chosen to match AlphaFold3.

quotes.text: trained with a data cutoff aligned with AlphaFold3 (2021-09-30)

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: No hard limit is stated; cost rises with the token count. The measured table runs from 500 tokens (6.1 GB peak memory, 17 s) to 4000 tokens and 40000 atoms (78.1 GB, 1424 s), and the code lowers precision above 2560 and 3840 tokens to avoid running out of memory.

facts.label: Weights licence
facts.value: Apache-2.0 for the open-source checkpoints: the README says the project including model parameters is Apache 2.0 and free for academic and commercial use. The protenix-v2 weights are an exception: they are proprietary and not released under any open-source licence.

quotes.text: The Protenix project including both code and model parameters is released under the [Apache 2.0 License](./LICENSE). It is free for both academic research and commercial use.
The model weights of Protenix-v2 are proprietary and confidential information of the rights holder, are not released under any open-source license

facts.label: Code licence
facts.value: Apache-2.0 (Apache License, Version 2.0), as declared in the repository and the LICENSE file.

facts.label: Access
facts.value: Code: https://github.com/bytedance/Protenix, installed with pip install protenix. Weights are fetched by the CLI when a model name is given; the sources read do not give a direct download URL. A hosted service is listed at https://protenix-server.com. The protenix-v2 weights are not open source.

run_guide.summary: Install the Protenix CLI and predict the structure of the example input with the open base checkpoint.
prerequisites: A GPU is assumed by the inference settings; the developers' table reports 6.1 GB peak memory for a 500-token input and 78.1 GB for 4000 tokens.
kalign and hmmer are needed for template and RNA MSA search, and are pre-installed only in the official Docker image.
Code and the open checkpoints are Apache-2.0 and free for academic and commercial use. The protenix-v2 weights are not open source.

steps.title: Install the CLI
steps.explanation: Installs the published Protenix package, which provides the protenix command. The README recommends the official PyPI index so the CLI matches the documented commands.

steps.title: Get the example input
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/bytedance/Protenix.git
cd Protenix
git checkout --detach 85767b811c40ed46e73a9b39519cf6bfca8701ba
steps.explanation: The prediction command reads examples/input.json from the repository. The clone, cd and checkout lines are added to get that file at the commit this page was written from; the README does not give them.

steps.title: Predict a structure
steps.explanation: The README's quick prediction command. It runs the open base checkpoint on the example protein chain and writes the results under ./output. Alignment search runs by default; add --use_msa false to skip it, as the instructions show.
